newsitem.title: FRANCE: French drinks duties up by 1.5 bln, "premixes" hit.
newsitem.headline: French drinks duties up by 1.5 bln, "premixes" hit.

text.p: France will raise 1.5 billion francs next year through higher excise duties on spirits and "premixes" -- prepared mixes of spirits and soda -- the government said on Monday.
Health Minister Herve Gaymard said he had insisted premixes were covered by the increase in excise duties given their popularity with young people.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said last week during the presentation of a 1997 budget that alcohol duties would rise by 1.2 billion francs.
The proceeds from the 17.1-percent increase in excise duties will be used to help reduce a deficit on the welfare system, the government said in a statement on Monday.
Tobacco duties are being raised by three billion francs, also to help pay for the welfare sytem.

The government on Monday presented the outlines of its plans to reduce the welfare deficit, to be covered by a special bill on financing for the welfare system. The special bill is expected to be debated by parliament on October 28 to 31.
In France, the welfare system is run separately from the core government budget.
